agent_final_message:
solution.py is done and verified on the remote RTX PRO 6000.

**Result:** `status: correct` (check.py PASS across all 5 shapes × 3 seeds × numeric-stress cases + the Hypothesis property suite), no forbidden ops, benchmark `peak_fraction 0.0222` (0.5–2 MB inputs, 13–82 µs/shape).

What it is: two custom CUDA kernels (torch `load_inline`, no CUB/Triton) — a per-block **bitonic merge tree** over 64-bit `(orderable_float<<32)|index` keys in shared memory, plus a per-row merge kernel; templates on the register-list size `M`, shift/mask-only indexing, in-place single-buffer tree, staged loads, and cached scratch buffers.

Measured facts worth recording: at these sizes the run is dominated by fixed costs, not the algorithm — a null kernel launch costs ~3.5 µs on this box and the input read is ~1 µs, so two launches alone cap peak_fraction near 0.11; the per-block merge tree is what separates shapes (a trivial k=1 tree runs at ~540 GB/s while an 8-level tree over the same 2 MB runs at ~80 GB/s). I confirmed the `M`-runtime→template change and the division→shift/in-place rewrite each helped (0.0160 → 0.0222), and that a further intra-run register-stage variant was inside run-to-run noise, so I kept the simpler verified tree. Out of practice runs (0 left); `solution.py` is exactly the kernel code that passed, with only dead scratch instrumentation removed.
